direction: V-tile (BV) size correction for chunk-recurrence kernel: uniform BV=min(64,V) replacing parent cs-dependent heuristic (BV=64 if BT<=64 else 32)
hypothesis: MCTS expands high-reward node opt-round-1 (mean reward 1.7403, visits 1). Parent used hand-tuned BV heuristic (BV=64 when BT<=64 else 32) which leaves headroom on chunk_size=128 shapes. Empirical sweep over all 8 shapes shows BV=64 is fastest on every shape incl. cs=128; fix = uniform BV=min(64,V).
design_summary: Round 2 MCTS expansion of opt-round-1. Fused chunk-recurrence kernel body preserved byte-for-byte; host V-tile BV made uniform BV=min(64,V). Offline empirical BV sweep of the actual parent kernel over all 8 task shapes (dense+varlen, cs 64/128) disproved the parent cs-dependent heuristic: BV=64 is fastest on EVERY shape, giving 1.46-1.72x on the four cs=128 cases where parent ran BV=32.
key_fixes: Replaced parent BV heuristic '64 if BT<=64 else 32' with uniform BV=min(64,V)
Kept D6 min() guard and V%BV==0 assertion; all shapes V=128 -> BV=64, NVT=2
Preserved fp32-ieee dot precision and multibuffer=True/unit_flag=True launch (D7)
bottlenecks_observed: cs=128 shapes were V-tile-suboptimal (BV=32) in parent: only 2.9-3.5x per-shape speedup
BV=128 never faster than BV=64 (UB pressure, D5)
Triton-Ascend num_warps/num_stages autotune unsupported; manual BV autotune reproduces BV=64 with ~7s/shape runtime cost -> not used
Residual cost is inherent serial chunk recurrence (grid parallelized by B*HV*NVT)

int32 scalar loop accumulator for varlen boh (avoid int32->int64 loop-carried type error)
